oshb:Ezek.1.11 (OSHB editorial note, single-witness: form-validity question, no reading changed)

newvals.P01-002|boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.2.1 וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י בֶּן אָדָם֙ עֲמֹ֣ד עַל רַגְלֶ֔יךָ וַאֲדַבֵּ֖ר אֹתָֽךְ (“He said to me, ‘Son of man, stand on your feet’” (web:Ezek.2.1)) opens the commission immediately after the vision's samekh-marked close at oshb:Ezek.1.28. The sending proper follows at 2:3, שׁוֹלֵ֨חַ אֲנִ֤י אֽוֹתְךָ֙ אֶל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Ezek.2.3) (“I send you to the children of Israel” (web:Ezek.2.3)), continuing into the messenger formula כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.2.4), embedded as reported speech rather than a fresh onset. Pe marks fall after 2:2 and 2:5, disclosed as intra-row sub-paragraph texture, not unit cuts. Close: 2:7, the refrain-form כִּ֥י מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.2.7) ('for they are rebellious'), with a pe recorded after it, before a fresh sub-onset address opens at 2:8.
newvals.P01-003|boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.2.8 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם … (WEB “But you, son of man, hear” (web:Ezek.2.8)) opens a fresh sub-onset immediately after the refrain-marked pe close at oshb:Ezek.2.7. The scroll appears at 2:9, וָאֶרְאֶ֕ה וְהִנֵּה יָ֖ד שְׁלוּחָ֣ה אֵלָ֑י וְהִנֵּה (oshb:Ezek.2.9) (“behold, a hand was stretched out to me” (web:Ezek.2.9)), and its inscription is read at 2:10, אֵלֶ֔יהָ קִנִ֥ים וָהֶ֖גֶה וָהִֽי (oshb:Ezek.2.10) ('lamentations, mourning, and woe'), with a samekh recorded after 2:10, disclosed as intra-row texture rather than a cut, since the eating that follows continues the same scroll scene: 3:1 reopens with a further 'he said to me,' אֱכוֹל֙ אֶת הַמְּגִלָּ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את (oshb:Ezek.3.1) ('eat this scroll'), intra-row, and the WEB chapter numeral falling at 2:10/3:1 is disclosed only as tier-4 texture, never as boundary evidence. Close: 3:3, וַתְּהִ֥י בְּפִ֖י כִּדְבַ֥שׁ לְמָתֽוֹק (oshb:Ezek.3.3) ('it was in my mouth as sweet as honey'), with a pe recorded after it, before the address turns from the scroll to the audience's character at 3:4.
newvals.P01-004|boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:4 לֶךְ בֹּא֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Ezek.3.4) ('go, get you to the house of Israel'), a fresh 'he said to me' turning from the scroll itself to the audience it will be spoken to; 3:7 characterizes them, כִּ֚י כָּל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל חִזְקֵי מֵ֥צַח וּקְשֵׁי לֵ֖ב הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.7) (“for all the house of Israel are obstinate and hard-hearted” (web:Ezek.3.7)). A pe is recorded after 3:9, כְּשָׁמִ֛יר חָזָ֥ק מִצֹּ֖ר נָתַ֣תִּי מִצְחֶ֑ךָ (“I have made your forehead as a diamond” (web:Ezek.3.9)), closing with a further rebellious-house refrain, כִּ֛י בֵּֽית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.9) (the third of six). That mark is disclosed but not read as the unit's own close: 3:10 reopens with “Moreover he said to me” (web:Ezek.3.10) on the same audience-description topic, and cutting there would leave 3:10-3:11 (2 verses, no word-event of its own) detached from the speech they continue. Close: 3:11, אִֽם יִשְׁמְע֖וּ וְאִם יֶחְדָּֽלוּ (oshb:Ezek.3.11) (“whether they will hear, or whether they will refuse” (web:Ezek.3.11)), immediately before the return-transport of 3:12 begins a distinct, vision-texture scene.
newvals.P01-005|boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:12 וַתִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי ר֔וּחַ (oshb:Ezek.3.12) (“Then the Spirit lifted me up” (web:Ezek.3.12)) begins the return-transport away from the plain-vision back to the exiles, distinct in texture from the preceding commissioning speech (no address, no imperative - narrated action). 3:14 carries the hand-of-YHWH construct, וְיַד יְהוָ֥ה עָלַ֖י חָזָֽקָה (oshb:Ezek.3.14) ('the hand of YHWH was strong upon me'); it is weighed and NOT read as a fresh vision onset here, in contrast to 1:3 and 3:22 - it sits inside a single continuous journey (lifted up → went in bitterness → came to Tel-abib) with no scene change around it, so it is disclosed as transit texture rather than a hard seam. Close: 3:15, וָאֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁ֛ם שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים מַשְׁמִ֥ים בְּתוֹכָֽם (oshb:Ezek.3.15) (“I sat there overwhelmed among them seven days” (web:Ezek.3.15)); no parashah mark is recorded at 3:15, which is not read as counterevidence against the seam. The gap this closes is temporal, not formulaic: 3:16 reopens on “At the end of seven days” (web:Ezek.3.16) with its own strict word-event.
newvals.P01-006|boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:16 carries the book's first strict word-event formula, וַיְהִ֕י מִקְצֵ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.3.16) (“At the end of seven days, Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Ezek.3.16)), a hard seam, since a strict word-event opens a new oracle and no unit runs across one (3:16 is one of the 39 strict-form verses and one of the 48 in the first-person family). A pe is recorded after this verse; the inventory does not carry intra-verse position, so no claim is made about whether the mark falls before or after 3:17's watchman charge, צֹפֶ֥ה נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.3.17) (“I have made you a watchman to the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.3.17)). A samekh follows 3:19, between the wicked-man case (3:18-19) and the righteous-man case (3:20-21); disclosed as an internal paragraph mark, not a unit cut, since both cases are one paired illustration of the same watchman charge and no fresh onset device stands at 3:20. Close: 3:21, at the second samekh, before the hand-of-YHWH reopens the scene at 3:22.
newvals.P01-007|boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:22 וַתְּהִ֥י עָלַ֛י שָׁ֖ם יַד יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.3.22) (“Yahweh’s hand was there on me” (web:Ezek.3.22)), the hand-of-YHWH construct read here as a genuine vision onset (contrast oshb:Ezek.3.14, where the construct accompanies the spirit carrying the prophet away, a transit rather than a new scene) because it opens a fresh scene: “Arise, go out into the plain” (web:Ezek.3.22). 3:25 announces that עֲבוֹתִ֔ים (oshb:Ezek.3.25) ('ropes') will be put on the prophet; the word recurs at 4:8 in the siege sign-act, across the 3:27/4:1 seam (accent_stripped tier: the same consonants and vowels under a different accent), so the muteness command and the sign-acts share a device, and that continuity is weighed here against the seam even though the unit boundary stands. 3:26 carries the fifth rebellious-house refrain, כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה. Close: 3:27, הַשֹּׁמֵ֤עַ יִשְׁמָע֙ וְהֶחָדֵ֣ל יֶחְדָּ֔ל כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.27) (“He who hears, let him hear; and he who refuses, let him refuse; for they are a rebellious house” (web:Ezek.3.27)) - the sixth verse in chapters 2-3 to name the rebellious house (sweep: 12 verses book-wide name it, six of them in chapters 2-3), and the parent P1's close; a samekh is recorded after this verse. Across the seam, 4:1 opens with וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ (oshb:Ezek.4.1) ('and you, son of man'), spliced at byte tier as the 3:27 clause is, and turns to the command to take a tile, the sub-onset that starts the sign-acts. The unit therefore stops at 3:27 and does not extend into 4:1; the seam's near side is closed by the refrain and the samekh after 3:27 (single witness), and its far side is opened by that sub-onset.
newvals.P01-007|strongest_rejected_alternative: Placing the P1/P2 parent seam at 3:15/3:16 instead of 3:27/4:1, on the strength of 3:16's own strict word-event and the seven-day close it answers. Weighed on the bytes, the onset side of that seam is strong: 3:16 sets מִקְצֵ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.3.16) (“At the end of seven days” (web:Ezek.3.16)) before its strict word-event, and a pe follows 3:16 itself (single witness), after the word-event verse rather than before it. Its close side is narrative: 3:15 ends the journey to the exiles on seven days of sitting among them, a report rather than a refrain. The rebellious-house refrain runs on both sides of 3:16 (sweep: of the six verses in chapters 2-3 that name the rebellious house, four stand before 3:16 and two after it), so a parent seam there would divide that series, whereas at 3:27/4:1 the series' sixth verse stands on the close side and the sub-onset of 4:1 on the onset side. The alternative is kept as a held question and not argued away, because the ropes of 3:25, taken up at 4:8, tie the muteness command (3:22-27) to the sign-acts (4:1-17) across the later seam.
newvals.P01-008|boundary_rationale: Onset: 4:1 וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ קַח לְךָ֣ לְבֵנָ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.4.1) (“You also, son of man, take a tile” (web:Ezek.4.1)), the 'and you, son of man' sub-onset that opens P2 (one of the book's 23 occurrences of that construction), immediately after the parent seam weighed at oshb:Ezek.3.27 above. The same siege-tile complex continues through the lying sign-acts at 4:4 and the food-rationing at 4:9 without a matching 'son of man' sub-onset at either point (both open with the bare 've'attah' alone), so all three stages read as one commanded symbolic act rather than three. At 4:8, וְהִנֵּ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי עָלֶ֖יךָ עֲבוֹתִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.4.8) (“Behold, I put ropes on you” (web:Ezek.4.8)) recurs the exact word from 3:25 on the far side of the parent seam, disclosed as continuity evidence the seam-assessment above already weighed. A second address at 4:16, בֶּן אָדָם֙ (oshb:Ezek.4.16), intensifies rather than restarts the act (“behold, I will break the staff of bread” (web:Ezek.4.16)). Close: 4:17, לְמַ֥עַן יַחְסְר֖וּ לֶ֣חֶם וָמָ֑יִם (oshb:Ezek.4.17) (“that they may lack bread and water” (web:Ezek.4.17)), with a pe recorded after it, before 5:1 opens a distinct sign-act with its own 'son of man' address.
newvals.P01-009|boundary_rationale: Onset: 5:1 וְאַתָּ֨ה בֶן אָדָ֜ם קַח לְךָ֣ חֶ֣רֶב חַדָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.5.1) (“You, son of man, take a sharp sword” (web:Ezek.5.1)), a fresh 'son of man' sub-onset distinct from 4:1's - a new symbolic object (sword/razor/hair) rather than a continuation of the siege-tile act. The messenger formula at 5:5, כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.5.5), opens the act's own interpretation rather than a competing unit (no refrain close intervenes between the hair-sign and its meaning). The oath at 5:11, חַי אָ֗נִי ('as I live'), with the utterance signature נְאֻם֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ (oshb:Ezek.5.11) attached mid-verse, marks an emphatic sub-onset of the verdict paragraph, not a unit boundary. The formula 'I, Yahweh, have spoken' recurs three times, at 5:13 (אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ (oshb:Ezek.5.13)), 5:15 (אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.5.15)) and 5:17 (אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.5.17)); the first two are paragraph-final rather than unit-final because no fresh onset device follows either (5:14 continues “Moreover I will make you a desolation” (web:Ezek.5.14) with no messenger formula or word-event reopening the address). Close: 5:17, with a pe recorded after it, before 6:1 opens with a fresh strict word-event. The verdict continues in two further 'therefore' messenger formulae addressing the same party: 5:7, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ezek.5.7) (2mp, 'therefore the Lord Yahweh says'), and 5:8, לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ezek.5.8) (2fs, 'therefore the Lord Yahweh says') — both verdict paragraphs inside the same interpretation, addressing Jerusalem and the people in her as one party, with no refrain standing before either (the samekh after 5:6, 5:7 and 5:9 are disclosed as intra-row texture, not unit-cutting seams). The verdict is bound to the sign-act itself by a byte-identical clause: 5:12 closes with the same words that close 5:2, וְחֶ֖רֶב אָרִ֥יק אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.5.2; oshb:Ezek.5.12) ('and I will draw a sword after them', sweep: 3 verses book-wide, the third at 12:14).
newvals.P01-010|boundary_rationale: Onset: 6:1 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.6.1) ('Yahweh's word came to me, saying'), a strict word-event, hard seam. 6:2 opens the oracle's direction with שִׂ֥ים פָּנֶ֖יךָ אֶל הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.6.2) (“set your face toward the mountains of Israel” (web:Ezek.6.2)). A 2mp recognition-family close occurs mid-unit at 6:7, וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.6.7) ('and you shall know that I am Yahweh'); it is disclosed but read as paragraph-final rather than unit-final, since 6:8 continues without a fresh onset device (“Yet I will leave a remnant” (web:Ezek.6.8)). Close: 6:10, the strict recognition formula וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.6.10) ('and they shall know that I am Yahweh'), with a pe recorded after it, immediately before a fresh messenger formula reopens the address at 6:11.
newvals.P01-010|strongest_rejected_alternative: Closing the unit at 6:7, the first recognition occurrence, rather than continuing to 6:10. Rejected because 6:8's “Yet I will leave a remnant” (web:Ezek.6.8) carries straight on from 6:7 with no messenger formula, word-event or address restarting the speech, so 6:7 reads as an internal refrain rather than the unit's own close.
